examples.source: To earn your badge for Quantum Chemistry with VQE … / Welcome to **Quantum chemistry with VQE**.
examples.suggested: لكسب شارتك في الكيمياء الكمومية باستخدام VQE
examples.translation: لكسب شارتك في الكيمياء الكمومية مع VQE … / مرحباً بك في **الكيمياء الكمومية باستخدام VQE**.
examples.why: The same English course title is rendered with باستخدام in the description and opening line but with مع at the exam section. The course name is a fixed label (it is the badge name learners will look for on Credly), so it should be byte-identical on every mention.

examples.source: you will learn the basic building blocks of VQE, options in its implementation, and a few applications
examples.suggested: ستتعلّم اللبنات الأساسية لـ VQE وخيارات تنفيذه وعدداً من تطبيقاته
examples.translation: ستتعلّم اللبنات الأساسية لـ VQE وخيارات تطبيقه وعدداً من تطبيقاته
examples.why: تطبيقه (implementation) and تطبيقاته (applications) sit three words apart and share the ط-ب-ق root, so the sentence appears to promise 'options for applying it and a number of its applications' — a jingle no Arabic technical writer would leave standing. تنفيذ is the normal rendering for 'implementation' and removes the collision. Also, English says 'a few applications' generically; تطبيقاته adds a possessive the source does not have.

examples.source: Your personal information is used to issue your badge and for program reporting and operational purposes.
examples.suggested: تُستخدم معلوماتك الشخصية لإصدار شارتك ولأغراض إعداد تقارير البرنامج والأغراض التشغيلية.
examples.translation: تُستخدم معلوماتك الشخصية لإصدار شارتك ولأغراض إعداد التقارير التشغيلية الخاصة بالبرنامج.
examples.why: The English lists two coordinated purposes — 'program reporting' and 'operational purposes'. The Arabic fuses them into a single purpose, 'preparing the programme's operational reports', by attaching التشغيلية as an adjective on التقارير. This narrows the declared scope of personal-data use in a privacy notice; it does not distort any technical content, but it is a dropped item rather than a rewording.

editor_note: Content-wise the translation is faithful throughout — I checked the variational-principle inequality, the little-endian/qubit-wise-commuting discussion (`IZIZ`/`ZZXZ` vs `ZZZZ`/`ZZZX`), the QPE O(1/ε) vs O(1/ε²) contrast, and the ADAPT-VQE/SQD/QSCI section, and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity or hallucinated claim; register is consistently informal singular (لاحظ، تذكّر، افترض أن مصفوفتك). What a native editor would change: (1) "span the space of all operators" is rendered "تُفرِّق الفضاء على جميع عوامل ذات بُعد معيّن" — تُفرِّق means "separates/scatters", not "spans" (تفرش/تمتدّ على/تولّد), and the indefinite "جميع عوامل" is ungrammatical; (2) "note the implication" becomes "لاحظ التداعي", where التداعي reads as psychological free-association rather than logical implication (المضمون/النتيجة المترتبة); (3) "operator" is split between عامل (§1, §1.1, §2.2) and مؤثّر (§3 step list, §4.2 ADAPT-VQE, the geometry answer) — glossed once as "عامل (مؤثّر)" so still identifiable, but inconsistent; likewise "fault tolerance" is "التسامح الخطأي" in §4.1 but "متسامحة مع الأخطاء" in the QPE section. (4) Several agreement/typo slips a native writer would not make: "ستُعرِّفك هذه الدرس", "القطرنة الدقيقة ليس خيارًا مطروحًا" and "حين لا يكون القطرنة الدقيقة ممكنًا" (fem. subject, masc. verb/predicate), "مصفوفة ذات N صفًا و N عمودًا", and "المصفوفة المراد قطرنةها" (should be قطرنتها). None of these mislead; they are polish-level.

examples.source: Because Pauli matrices (plus the identity: X, Y, Z, and I) span the space of all operators of a given dimension, we are guaranteed that we can write our matrix of interest as a weighted sum of Pauli operators
examples.suggested: ولأن مصفوفات باولي (مع مصفوفة الهوية: X وY وZ وI) تفرش فضاء جميع العوامل ذات بُعد معيّن، فمن المضمون أن نستطيع كتابة مصفوفتنا موضع الاهتمام كمجموع موزون لعوامل باولي
examples.translation: ولأن مصفوفات باولي (مع الهوية: X و Y و Z و I) تُفرِّق الفضاء على جميع عوامل ذات بُعد معيّن، فمن المضمون أن نستطيع كتابة مصفوفتنا موضع الاهتمام كمجموع موزون لعوامل باولي
examples.why: 'تُفرِّق' means to separate/scatter, not to span; the standard renderings are تفرش / تمتدّ على / تولّد. The construction 'الفضاء على جميع عوامل' also drops the definite article and garbles 'the space OF all operators'. The following clause rescues the meaning, so it confuses rather than misleads.

examples.source: But note the implication: the variational state that produces the lowest-energy expectation value *is* the best estimate of the true ground state.
examples.suggested: لكن لاحظ ما يترتّب على ذلك: الحالة التباينية التي تُنتج أدنى قيمة توقّع للطاقة *هي* أفضل تقدير للحالة الأساسية الحقيقية.
examples.translation: لكن لاحظ التداعي: الحالة التباينية التي تُنتج أدنى قيمة توقّع للطاقة *هي* أفضل تقدير للحالة الأساسية الحقيقية.
examples.why: 'التداعي' carries the sense of collapse or (in psychology) free association; it is not the Arabic for a logical 'implication'. A technical writer would use ما يترتّب على ذلك / المضمون / النتيجة.

examples.source: operator (An operator: Often a Hamiltonian…; Map problem to quantum circuits and operators; …the operator from a predefined pool…)
examples.suggested: pick one rendering (عامل, since that is what §1–§2.3 use consistently) and apply it to the Qiskit-patterns step list, the geometry answer and the ADAPT-VQE paragraph
examples.translation: __عامل (مؤثّر)__ … -__الخطوة 1__: تحويل المسألة إلى دوائر كمية ومؤثّرات … تختار المؤثّر من مجموعة مُعرَّفة مسبقًا
examples.why: Within-file split between عامل and مؤثّر for the same concept. The first-use gloss 'عامل (مؤثّر)' keeps it identifiable, so it is a polish issue, not a comprehension one.

examples.source: This lesson will introduce… / a matrix with N rows and N columns… exact diagonalization is not an option / the matrix to be diagonalized
examples.suggested: ستُعرِّفك هذا الدرس… / بمصفوفة ذات N صف وN عمود… أن القطرنة الدقيقة ليست خيارًا مطروحًا / المصفوفة المراد قطرنتها
examples.translation: ستُعرِّفك هذه الدرس بخوارزمية… / بمصفوفة ذات N صفًا و N عمودًا… أن القطرنة الدقيقة ليس خيارًا مطروحًا / المصفوفة المراد قطرنةها
examples.why: Gender-agreement slips (درس and قطرنة), a broken tamyeez after ذات, and a misspelling of قطرنتها. Each is small, but they cluster and mark the text as unedited rather than natively written.

examples.source: approaching large scale fault tolerance / QPE requires fault-tolerant quantum computers
examples.suggested: use تحمّل الأخطاء / متحمّلة للأخطاء in both places
examples.translation: تقترب من التسامح الخطأي واسع النطاق / يتطلّب QPE حواسيب كمية متسامحة مع الأخطاء
examples.why: 'التسامح الخطأي' is a non-standard coinage and is inconsistent with the 'متسامحة مع الأخطاء' used a few paragraphs later for the same concept; both are recognizable, so MINOR.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked the whole SQD post-processing half (configuration recovery, the N=2 / x=|1000⟩ worked example, the occupancy tables, the "first iteration vs subsequent iterations" list, and the 24 mH vs 1.6 mH chemical-accuracy discussion) and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucinated claim; the informal register (زِد، اختر، دائرتك، حاسوبك) holds. What a native editor would change is terminology consistency: "configuration" is split between التكوينات (the step-4 outline, lines 30/41: "الاسترداد الذاتي للتكوينات") and التهيئات everywhere in §4 ("استرداد التهيئة"), and "ansatz" is النموذج الأولي throughout but suddenly "دالة LUCJ الأنساتز" at line 279; "spatial orbital" is مدار مكاني in §1 but مدار فراغي at line 515. There are also a few local roughnesses: the heavy-hex bullet "المدارات ذات الفهرس المضاعف للـ $4$-الأول" (line 145) is garbled Arabic that only the 0/4/8 examples rescue, "كل مدار آخر" (line 146) is a literal calque of "every other orbital" that in Arabic reads "each other orbital", and "مدير تمريرات مُرحَّل" (lines 224–225) is a shaky rendering of "staged pass manager". Minor mechanical slips: the typo "وقطرنةه" (line 33, should be وقطرنته), "قد يبدو كتلة إعداد" (line 118, gender agreement) and the frontmatter "يُطبَّق القطرنة … القائم" (line 4).

examples.source: self-consistent configuration recovery loop / configuration recovery
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering of "configuration" (التهيئات, the dominant one in §4) and use it in the step-4 outline too; also restore "ذاتية الاتساق" in line 30, which currently reads only as "self-recovery".
examples.translation: حلقة الاسترداد الذاتي للتكوينات … استرداد التكوينات (lines 30, 41) vs استرداد التهيئة / التهيئات ذاتية الاتساق (§4 throughout)
examples.why: The same core concept is named two different ways in the same file, and the outline entry additionally drops the "self-consistent" qualifier that the whole of §4.1 is built on.

examples.source: Sampling the LUCJ ansatz in the computational basis generates a pool of noisy configurations
examples.suggested: أخذ عينات من النموذج الأولي LUCJ في الأساس الحسابي…
examples.translation: أخذ عينات من دالة LUCJ الأنساتز في الأساس الحسابي يولّد مجموعة من التهيئات الضوضائية
examples.why: "ansatz" is rendered النموذج الأولي consistently in §1–§2; the one-off transliteration "دالة … الأنساتز" (plus the spurious "دالة") breaks that convention mid-document.

examples.source: The α-β interactions are kept between every 4-th indexed (such as the 0th, 4th, and 8th) spin orbitals
examples.suggested: تُبقى تفاعلات α-β بين مدارات الدوران التي تكون فهارسها من مضاعفات 4 (مثل 0 و4 و8)
examples.translation: تُحفظ تفاعلات $\alpha$-$\beta$ بين المدارات ذات الفهرس المضاعف للـ $4$-الأول (مثل الفهرس 0 و4 و8)
examples.why: "ذات الفهرس المضاعف للـ 4-الأول" is not parsable Arabic; only the parenthetical 0/4/8 lets the reader recover the rule.

examples.source: Every other orbital, such as 0th, 2nd, and 4th indexed orbitals, becomes nearest neighbors
examples.suggested: يصبح كل مدار ثانٍ (أي المدارات 0 و2 و4 …) أقرب جار
examples.translation: كل مدار آخر، مثل المدارات ذات الفهرس 0 و2 و4، يصبح أقرب جار
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English idiom: "كل مدار آخر" reads as "each other orbital", not "every second orbital"; a native technical writer would write كل مدار ثانٍ.

examples.source: Project and diagonalize the molecular Hamiltonian over each sampled subspace.
examples.suggested: إسقاط الهاميلتوني الجزيئي وقطرنته على كل فضاء جزئي مأخوذ بالعينات.
examples.translation: إسقاط الهاميلتوني الجزيئي وقطرنةه على كل فضاء جزئي من العينات.
examples.why: "قطرنةه" is a spelling error for قطرنته (tā' marbūṭa retained before the pronoun suffix).

editor_note: No semantic inversions, dropped caveats or hallucinated claims: the SQD sequentiality paragraph, the four Qiskit-pattern stages and the Slurm dependency narrative all track the English faithfully, and the informal register (افترض أنك تنمذج، هل ستستخدم، دائرتك) holds throughout. The one substantive editorial defect is that "observable" is rendered as "قياس" in every occurrence (lines 24, 184, 214, 232, 279), which is the same word the file already uses for "measurement" (مجموعة من القياسات، قياسات كمومية) — so the Estimator's "expectation value of an observable" becomes "القيمة التوقعية لقياس" and the saved observable file becomes "القياس", blurring the very Sampler-vs-Estimator distinction the lesson teaches; the conventional rendering (المؤثر القابل للرصد / الكمية القابلة للقياس) would keep the two apart. Smaller slips: "جانباً نماذج البرمجة الكمومية" instead of "إلى جانب"; "هذه البنية الفرعية الشجرية" for "this branch-like structure" (reads "sub-structure", should be البنية المتفرعة); "في الفصل الأخير" for "in the last chapter" (reads "the final chapter" rather than the previous one); plus a typo "سنستيرد" for "سنستورد" and gender disagreement in "القطرنة الكلاسيكي".

examples.source: Estimator allows you to estimate the expectation value of an observable for a system in the state prepared by your quantum circuit.
examples.suggested: يتيح لك Estimator تقدير القيمة التوقعية لمؤثر قابل للرصد (observable) لنظام في الحالة التي تُحضِّرها دائرتك الكمومية.
examples.translation: يتيح لك Estimator تقدير القيمة التوقعية لقياس لنظام في الحالة التي يُحضِّرها دائرتك الكمومية.
examples.why: "observable" is rendered with the same word the file uses for "measurement" (القياسات), collapsing the observable/measurement distinction that the Sampler-vs-Estimator lesson (and its check-your-understanding item) rests on. Recognizable in context, so MINOR, but a native technical editor would separate the two terms.

examples.source: Using these two models alongside quantum programming models, one can express almost any hybrid quantum-classical workflow of any complexity.
examples.suggested: باستخدام هذين النموذجَين إلى جانب نماذج البرمجة الكمومية، يمكن للمرء التعبير عن أي سير عمل هجين كمومي-كلاسيكي تقريباً، مهما بلغ تعقيده.
examples.translation: باستخدام هذين النموذجَين جانباً نماذج البرمجة الكمومية، يمكن للمرء التعبير عن تقريباً أي سير عمل هجين كمومي-كلاسيكي بأي تعقيد.
examples.why: "جانباً" is not the Arabic for "alongside" (needs إلى جانب), and the fronted "تقريباً أي" is a direct calque of English "almost any" that a native writer would place after the noun.

examples.source: This branch-like structure is orchestrated and executed by the scheduler.
examples.suggested: هذه البنية المتفرعة يُنسِّقها المجدوِل وينفّذها.
examples.translation: هذه البنية الفرعية الشجرية يُنسِّقها المجدوِل وينفّذها.
examples.why: "البنية الفرعية" means "sub-structure", not "branch-like"; the intended sense (branching/tree-shaped) is المتفرعة. Harmless in context but wrong wording.

examples.source: ...which implements the Qiskit pattern (map, optimize, execute, and post-process) within Slurm that we learned in the last chapter.
examples.suggested: ...داخل Slurm الذي تعلمناه في الفصل السابق.
examples.translation: ...يُنفِّذ نمط Qiskit (تعيين، تحسين، تنفيذ، ومعالجة لاحقة) داخل Slurm الذي تعلمناه في الفصل الأخير.
examples.why: "الفصل الأخير" reads as "the final chapter" of the course; the English "last chapter" means the preceding one — a small pointer error for a learner navigating the course.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout and the core terminology is correct and consistent (ansatz→الأنساتز, variational form→الشكل التغايري, qubit→كيوبت, entanglement→تشابك, expectation value→القيمة التوقعية, Hamiltonian→هاميلتوني، cost function→دالة التكلفة), so nothing here would teach a false concept. What a native technical editor would still change: (1) the hedge in "create entanglement between them, which CAN BE important for simulating complex quantum systems" is strengthened to "وهو أمر بالغ الأهمية" ("which is extremely important"), losing the English's deliberate caution; (2) "The syntax is the same as `NLocal`" is softened to "الصياغة مشابهة لـ`NLocal`" ("similar to"), which is weaker than the source's flat claim of identity; (3) "the runtime complexity of search algorithms" drops the "runtime" qualifier ("تعقيد خوارزميات البحث"). Plus a frontmatter gender-agreement slip ("تشرح هذه الدرس" for the masculine الدرس) and the awkward calque "وحدتين وحدويتين" for "two unitaries" in an image alt (conventional Arabic is "مؤثران وحدويان"). Register is correctly informal throughout (لديك، تذكر، تعلمت).

examples.source: the local gates can act on neighboring qubits and create entanglement between them, which can be important for simulating complex quantum systems.
examples.suggested: ... وهو ما قد يكون مهماً لمحاكاة الأنظمة الكمومية المعقدة.
examples.translation: البوابات المحلية تتفاعل مع الكيوبتات المجاورة وتُنشئ تشابكاً بينها، وهو أمر بالغ الأهمية لمحاكاة الأنظمة الكمومية المعقدة.
examples.why: The English hedge "can be important" becomes an unqualified superlative "بالغ الأهمية" (extremely important); the modality is strengthened. Also "act on" is rendered "تتفاعل مع" (interact with) rather than "تعمل على".

examples.source: The syntax is the same as `NLocal`, but there are some differences.
examples.suggested: الصياغة هي نفسها المستخدمة مع `NLocal`، لكن هناك بعض الاختلافات.
examples.translation: الصياغة مشابهة لـ`NLocal` مع بعض الاختلافات.
examples.why: "the same as" is softened to "مشابهة" (similar to). The English deliberately says the syntax is identical and only then flags exceptions; the Arabic weakens the base claim the learner is meant to carry over.

examples.source: the runtime complexity of search algorithms, and others alike, grows exponentially with this dimensionality
examples.suggested: تعقيد زمن التشغيل لخوارزميات البحث وما شابهها يزداد أسياً مع هذه الأبعاد
examples.translation: تعقيد خوارزميات البحث وما شابهها يزداد أسياً مع هذه الأبعاد
examples.why: "runtime" is dropped, leaving a generic "complexity" — the specific claim about time complexity is blurred.

examples.source: This lesson explains what an ansatz is and how it differs from the reference state.
examples.suggested: يشرح هذا الدرس ما هو الأنساتز وكيف يختلف عن الحالة المرجعية.
examples.translation: تشرح هذه الدرس ما هو الأنساتز وكيف يختلف عن حالة المرجع.
examples.why: Gender-agreement error in the frontmatter description: الدرس is masculine, so it must be "يشرح هذا الدرس", not "تشرح هذه الدرس".

examples.source: A circuit diagram showing two unitaries: one preparing the reference state and another preparing the ansatz.
examples.suggested: رسم تخطيطي للدائرة يوضح مؤثرين وحدويين: أحدهما يُحضّر الحالة المرجعية والآخر يُحضّر الأنساتز.
examples.translation: رسم تخطيطي للدائرة يوضح وحدتين وحدويتين: إحداهما تُحضّر حالة المرجع والأخرى تُحضّر الأنساتز.
examples.why: "وحدتين وحدويتين" is a redundant calque ("two unitary units"); the conventional Arabic for a unitary in this sense is "مؤثر وحدوي". A native technical writer would not write this.

editor_note: The translation is faithful in substance across the long simulator and quantum-safe sections (all figures preserved: 2^100, 10^30, 30–35 qubit, 250+, 2800+, 600,000+; the "لا يمكنك تنفيذ جميع العمليات الكلاسيكية" / "التوازي الأسي" caveat survives intact), so nothing rises to a misleading claim. But six editorial slips remain. (1) "definitively demonstrate" is rendered "إثبات بيانياً" ("demonstrate graphically") — a wrong adverb that weakens the quantum-advantage criterion; it should be "بشكل قاطع". (2) The appositive in "replacing the bit, the base unit of information" is mis-parsed into an instrumental: "استبدال البت بوحدة المعلومات الأساسية" reads "replacing the bit WITH the base unit of information", which is incoherent. (3) "the sign and magnitude of each coefficient" becomes "إشارة ومعامل كل معامل" — "magnitude" rendered as "معامل" (coefficient), producing a self-referential nonsense phrase; it should be "مقدار". (4) Security terminology drifts: "post-quantum cryptographic standard" → "معيار التشفير الكمومي ما بعد الكم" injects "الكمومي" (quantum cryptography, a different field), and "standardization" → "التقنين" (rationing/legislation) instead of "التقييس". (5) Register: the file is consistently informal singular (تكون قادراً، مهاراتك، انقر) except the Responsible-Computing paragraph, which switches to formal plural ("بوصفكم أعضاء… تتخذون… نأمل أن تشاركوا"). (6) "Becoming quantum ready/safe" is rendered with the philosophical noun "الصيرورة" ("الصيرورة مستعداً للكم", "الصيرورة آمناً كمومياً") — stiff calque no native technical writer would use.

examples.source: when we can definitively demonstrate, in certain use cases, a significant performance advantage over classical computers
examples.suggested: حين نستطيع الإثبات القاطع، في حالات استخدام معينة، لميزة أداء كبيرة على الحواسيب الكلاسيكية
examples.translation: حين نستطيع إثبات بيانياً، في حالات استخدام معينة، ميزة أداء كبيرة على الحواسيب الكلاسيكية
examples.why: ‘بيانياً’ means ‘graphically/diagrammatically’, not ‘definitively’. It replaces the rigor qualifier on the quantum-advantage criterion with an unrelated (and much weaker) one.

examples.source: Quantum computing is completely different from conventional computing, right down to replacing the bit, the base unit of information.
examples.suggested: … حتى إنها تستبدل البت، وهو وحدة المعلومات الأساسية.
examples.translation: الحوسبة الكمومية مختلفة اختلافاً جذرياً عن الحوسبة التقليدية، حتى في استبدال البت بوحدة المعلومات الأساسية.
examples.why: The English appositive (‘the bit, [which is] the base unit of information’) is read as an instrumental ‘بـ’, so the Arabic says the bit is replaced BY the base unit of information — an incoherent statement about what quantum computing changes.

examples.source: you would need to record the sign and magnitude of each coefficient
examples.suggested: إذ يتعين عليك تسجيل إشارة كل معامل ومقداره
examples.translation: إذ يتعين عليك تسجيل إشارة ومعامل كل معامل
examples.why: ‘magnitude’ is rendered ‘معامل’ (coefficient), producing the circular phrase ‘the sign and coefficient of each coefficient’; the reason more bits are needed is lost.

examples.source: …as part of its post-quantum cryptographic standard… submitted three new digital signature schemes as candidates for standardization
examples.suggested: …ضمن معيار التشفير ما بعد الكمومي… كمرشحين للتقييس
examples.translation: …ضمن معيار التشفير الكمومي ما بعد الكم… كمرشحين للتقنين
examples.why: ‘التشفير الكمومي’ (quantum cryptography) is a different field from post-quantum cryptography, and ‘التقنين’ means rationing/legislating rather than standardization (‘التقييس’).

examples.source: As members of the quantum computing community, you make important decisions… We hope that you will participate…
examples.suggested: بوصفك عضواً في مجتمع الحوسبة الكمومية، تتخذ قرارات مهمة… نأمل أن تشارك…
examples.translation: بوصفكم أعضاء في مجتمع الحوسبة الكمومية، تتخذون قرارات مهمة… نأمل أن تشاركوا…
examples.why: The rest of the file addresses the reader with informal singular (‘تكون قادراً’, ‘مهاراتك’, ‘انقر’); this paragraph switches to formal plural, breaking the file's convention.

editor_note: The translation is faithful on all the load-bearing technical content — key-space sizes, the AES-256 security margin (9 de 14 rondas → margen de 5), the Grover halving (128 bits → 64 bits), confusión/difusión, IND-CPA and the OTP caveat are all correct, and the informal register ("Observa que...", "Consulta [Tomoiaga et al.]") holds throughout. What a native editor would still change: "quantum-safe products" is rendered "productos cuánticos seguros" (line 338), which parses as "secure quantum products" rather than "seguros frente a la computación cuántica" — the very concept the course is named after. Two small quantifier/qualifier slips soften or restate the English: "much more practically efficient than an OTP" becomes "esencialmente más eficientes en la práctica" (line 276), and "a specified number of rounds" becomes "un número fijo de rondas" (line 284), which sits awkwardly beside the later RC5/RC6 sentence about a customizable "número de rondas". There is also an agreement error, "ninguna dos operaciones de cifrado utilicen el mismo par clave-IV" (line 300), a softened claim in the VPN bullet ("which aim to provide" → "que ofrecen", line 235), and an inconsistent "computador cuántico" vs "computadora clásica/cuántica" split across lines 346/358/362/376. None of these would teach a learner a false concept.

examples.source: with the adoption of quantum-safe products poised to secure our information against the looming threat of quantum computing advancements
examples.suggested: donde la adopción de productos seguros frente a la computación cuántica (quantum-safe) apunta a proteger nuestra información...
examples.translation: donde la introducción de productos cuánticos seguros tiene como objetivo proteger nuestra información contra la amenaza inminente de los avances en la computación cuántica
examples.why: "productos cuánticos seguros" reads as "secure quantum products"; quantum-safe means resistant to quantum attack, and this is the course's central term.

examples.source: feature large key space sizes while also being much more practically efficient than an OTP
examples.suggested: ...siendo al mismo tiempo mucho más eficientes en la práctica que un OTP
examples.translation: tienen grandes espacios de claves, siendo al mismo tiempo esencialmente más eficientes en la práctica que un OTP
examples.why: "much more" is rendered as "esencialmente" (essentially), which reads as a hedge rather than the strong quantitative contrast the English draws with the one-time pad.

examples.source: performs a specified number of rounds of transformations to yield a ciphertext block
examples.suggested: realiza un número determinado de rondas de transformaciones...
examples.translation: realiza un número fijo de rondas de transformaciones para producir un bloque de texto cifrado
examples.why: "specified" → "fijo" implies the round count is inherent to SPNs, which conflicts with the later RC5/RC6 sentence describing a configurable "número de rondas".

examples.source: with the additional requirement that no two encryption operations use the same key-IV pair
examples.suggested: con el requisito adicional de que dos operaciones de cifrado nunca utilicen el mismo par clave-IV
examples.translation: con el requisito adicional de que ninguna dos operaciones de cifrado utilicen el mismo par clave-IV
examples.why: "ninguna dos" is an agreement error and a direct calque of English "no two"; no native technical writer would produce it.

examples.source: VPN technologies, which aim to provide confidential communication channels free from eavesdropping
examples.suggested: Las tecnologías VPN, cuyo objetivo es ofrecer canales de comunicación confidenciales libres de escuchas
examples.translation: Las tecnologías VPN, que ofrecen canales de comunicación confidenciales libres de escuchas
examples.why: "aim to provide" is an intentional hedge; "que ofrecen" turns it into an unqualified assertion that VPNs do deliver eavesdropping-free channels.

examples.source: quantum computer / classical computer
examples.suggested: pick one of computador/computadora and use it for both classical and quantum throughout
examples.translation: "computador cuántico" (346, 362, 364, 370) vs "computadora clásica" (358, 362) and "computadoras cuánticas" (tooltips 376, 378)
examples.why: Within-file gender/form split on the same noun; recognizable but inconsistent for a single lesson.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no hallucinated claims; the CNOT truth table, the 75%/|0⟩ Born-rule example, the Little-Endian caveat, the non-factorizability argument for the Bell state and the depth-4/depth-5 statements all track the English exactly, and the informal "tú" register holds ("Aprenderás", "Haz clic", "Ten en cuenta"). Two things a native technical editor would still change. (1) In Exercise 2 "shallowest possible circuit" is rendered "el circuito más plano posible" / "la profundidad del circuito cuántico más plano es 5" — "plano" means *flat*, not *shallow*; the field says "de menor profundidad" or "menos profundo", especially jarring because "profundidad" appears in the same sentence. (2) Section 3.3's closing paragraph stacks two consecutive concessive "Aunque" clauses ("Aunque no se simuló ruido aquí... Aunque esperamos aproximadamente una distribución 50-50"), where the English varies its connectives ("Although... So while..."); the repetition reads as MT rhythm rather than native technical prose.

examples.source: Write code to prepare this state with the shallowest possible circuit. The depth of the shallowest quantum circuit is 5, including the measurement gates.
examples.suggested: Escribe código para preparar este estado con el circuito de menor profundidad posible. La profundidad del circuito cuántico menos profundo es 5, incluyendo las puertas de medición.
examples.translation: Escribe código para preparar este estado con el circuito más plano posible. La profundidad del circuito cuántico más plano es 5, incluyendo las puertas de medición.
examples.why: "shallow" applied to circuit depth is "de poca/menor profundidad" or "menos profundo" in Spanish; "plano" means flat and is not the domain term. Recognizable from the surrounding "profundidad", so not misleading, but it is the wrong technical word and it clashes with "circuitos con poca profundidad" used correctly a few paragraphs earlier (§4.4).

examples.source: Although noise has not been simulated here, the states are still probabilistic. So while we expect roughly a 50-50 distribution, we will rarely find exactly that.
examples.suggested: Aunque no se simuló ruido aquí, los estados siguen siendo probabilísticos. Por eso, si bien esperamos una distribución de aproximadamente 50-50, rara vez la obtendremos exacta.
examples.translation: Aunque no se simuló ruido aquí, los estados siguen siendo probabilísticos. Aunque esperamos aproximadamente una distribución 50-50, rara vez la encontraremos exactamente.
examples.why: Two back-to-back "Aunque" clauses lose the English discourse link ("So while..."), which marks a consequence, not a second concession. A native technical writer would vary the connective; the current pair reads as machine rhythm.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: the Trotterization derivation, the commuting/non-commuting argument, the Ising Hamiltonian description, the N=20 vs N=70 setups and all activity instructions match the English faithfully, and the informal "tú" register holds throughout ("Inténtalo por tu cuenta", "Desplázate hacia abajo", "Ten en cuenta"). What a native technical editor would change is consistency and polish: the course concept "utility-scale" is rendered two ways — "a escala de utilidad" in the H1 heading but "a escala utilitaria" in the closing line — and "target hardware" alternates between "hardware objetivo" (Paso 2, ~line 605) and "hardware de destino" (3.2/3.3, ~lines 770/799); "quantum computer" alternates between "computador cuántico" (~line 39) and "computadora cuántica" (~line 691). There is also a clumsy repetition "en términos de términos de Pauli ponderados" (~line 134), an accent typo "recópilalos" for "recopílalos" (~line 772), the calque "circuito superficial" for "shallow circuit" where "circuito de poca profundidad" is the field's term (~line 847), and "near-term quantum devices" flattened to "dispositivos cuánticos actuales" (~line 71), which loses the near-future sense. None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: Utility-scale experiment II … your utility-scale quantum journey
examples.suggested: Use "a escala de utilidad" in both places (closing: "…en tu camino por la computación cuántica a escala de utilidad")
examples.translation: Experimento a escala de utilidad II … tu camino hacia la computación cuántica a escala utilitaria
examples.why: The course's signature concept is rendered two different ways in the same file (heading vs. closing line); "utilitaria" also drifts toward "utilitarian" rather than "utility-scale".

examples.source: Optimize for target hardware / Execute on target hardware
examples.suggested: Pick one — e.g. "hardware objetivo" — and use it in all three Qiskit-patterns step headings
examples.translation: Optimización para el hardware objetivo … Optimizar para el hardware de destino … Ejecutar en el hardware de destino
examples.why: The same Qiskit-patterns step label is rendered two ways within one file, so the reader cannot tell whether Section 2 and Section 3 are describing the same step.

examples.source: a sparse representation of an operator in terms of weighted Pauli terms
examples.suggested: una representación dispersa de un operador como suma de términos de Pauli ponderados
examples.translation: una representación dispersa de un operador en términos de términos de Pauli ponderados
examples.why: "en términos de términos" is an accidental echo produced by translating "in terms of" literally; no Spanish technical writer would leave it.

examples.source: compare the hardware (default and shallow circuit) results with the MPS simulator
examples.suggested: circuito predeterminado y circuito de poca profundidad
examples.translation: comparar los resultados del hardware (circuito predeterminado y circuito superficial) con el simulador MPS
examples.why: "shallow circuit" is a depth concept (profundidad 208 → 7 in the printed output); "superficial" is a calque that reads as "cursory/lacking substance" rather than "low-depth".

examples.source: Transpile the circuits and gather them in a list.
examples.suggested: Transpila los circuitos y reúnelos en una lista.
examples.translation: Transpila los circuitos y recópilalos en una lista.
examples.why: "recópilalos" is misaccented (correct form is "recopílalos"), and "reunir" matches the parallel sentence already used in Section 2 ("los reunimos en una lista").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I found no semantic inversion, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucination; the technically dense passages (transpiled two-qubit depth of 80+, coherence 200–300 µs on Heron r3, the "quantum computers have no addressable memory" paragraph, the circuit-depth-9 layer breakdown) all track the English exactly, and the informal "tú" register holds (conocerás, deduce, Asegúrate). The defects are surface-level. (1) The `<IBMVideo title=...>` string on line 17 is still GERMAN ("In diesem Video beschreibt Iskandar Sitdikov wichtige Kennzahlen für Rechenressourcen…") — a visible, untranslated pivot-language leftover, and the same German pivot shows in the capitalized "Dynamical Decoupling", "Layer Fidelity", "Pauli-2-Design", "Heron-r3". (2) "circuit cutting/knitting" is rendered as the ungrammatical calque "el circuito Cutting" / "El circuito Knitting" (noun order inverted; Spanish convention is "corte de circuitos (circuit cutting)"). (3) Spelling error "Como se menciónó anteriormente" (double accent; should be "mencionó"). (4) The first Check-your-understanding prompt is malformed as a question: "…de los diferentes enfoques de escalamiento: ¿escalamiento vertical y horizontal?" — the source is a plain imperative, not an interrogative. (5) "no interleaved allocation" → "asignación entrelazada", which collides with "entrelazamiento" (entanglement) used for gates elsewhere in the same file; "intercalada" avoids the false friend. Also minor: stray trailing comma in the answer "(c) Asignación/Scheduling,", and "cannot be re-ordered to be parallel" loses "to be parallel" ("no pueden reordenarse sin cambiar la operación lógica").

examples.source: <IBMVideo id="134680652" title="In this video, Iskandar Sitdikov describes important measures of computing resources that apply to simple systems like a laptop all the way up to heterogeneous HPC environments"/>
examples.suggested: title="En este video, Iskandar Sitdikov describe medidas importantes de los recursos de cómputo, desde sistemas sencillos como una computadora portátil hasta entornos HPC heterogéneos"
examples.translation: <IBMVideo id="134680652" title="In diesem Video beschreibt Iskandar Sitdikov wichtige Kennzahlen für Rechenressourcen – von einfachen Systemen wie einem Laptop bis hin zu heterogenen HPC-Umgebungen"/>
examples.why: The video title is user-visible text left in GERMAN, not Spanish — a pivot-language leftover. The same German pivot explains the German-style capitalizations elsewhere (Dynamical Decoupling, Layer Fidelity, Pauli-2-Design).

examples.source: Circuit cutting is the process of breaks down large quantum tasks into smaller, manageable sub-tasks … Circuit knitting refers to the process that comes after circuit cutting
examples.suggested: …técnicas como el corte y recomposición de circuitos (circuit cutting/knitting). El corte de circuitos (circuit cutting) se refiere al proceso de dividir … La recomposición de circuitos (circuit knitting) se refiere al proceso posterior
examples.translation: se pueden emplear técnicas como el circuito Cutting/Knitting. El circuito Cutting se refiere al proceso de dividir grandes tareas cuánticas … El circuito Knitting se refiere al proceso posterior
examples.why: "El circuito Cutting" inverts the head noun — it reads as "the Cutting circuit", i.e. a kind of circuit, rather than a technique applied to circuits. Recognizable but clearly non-native; a Spanish technical writer would write "corte de circuitos" with the English term in parentheses.

examples.source: Use the descriptions above to infer some advantages and disadvantages of the different scaling approaches (vertical and horizontal).
examples.suggested: A partir de las descripciones anteriores, deduce algunas ventajas y desventajas de los diferentes enfoques de escalamiento (vertical y horizontal).
examples.translation: A partir de las descripciones anteriores, deduce algunas ventajas y desventajas de los diferentes enfoques de escalamiento: ¿escalamiento vertical y horizontal?
examples.why: The parenthetical gloss was converted into a dangling question ("¿escalamiento vertical y horizontal?") that asks nothing; the source sentence is an imperative. Grammatically broken as a question and confusing as an exercise prompt.

examples.source: Currently there is no interleaved allocation of mixed resources.
examples.suggested: Actualmente no existe una asignación intercalada de recursos mixtos.
examples.translation: No existe actualmente una asignación entrelazada de recursos mixtos.
examples.why: "Entrelazada" is a defensible general-computing rendering of "interleaved", but in this file "entrelazamiento"/"puertas de entrelazamiento" carry the quantum-entanglement sense, so the collision invites a wrong reading. "Intercalada" is unambiguous.

examples.source: As mentioned earlier, each quantum gate and each delay time between operations comes with noise…
examples.suggested: Como se mencionó anteriormente, cada puerta cuántica y cada tiempo de espera entre operaciones introduce ruido…
examples.translation: Como se menciónó anteriormente, cada puerta cuántica y cada tiempo de espera entre operaciones introduce ruido…
examples.why: "menciónó" carries two accents — a straight spelling error in the Spanish verb form (correct: "mencionó").

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — the distance-3 claim, the n = m + r accounting ("Cada generador duplica el tamaño del espacio de código, mientras que cada cadena de verificación de paridad lo divide a la mitad"), the min(j,k) correction bound, and the D_Z ⊆ C_X ⟺ D_X ⊆ C_Z condition all survive intact, and core terms are consistent (palabra código, cadena de verificación de paridad, generador de estabilizador Z/X, espacio de código, código dual). Two spots a native editor would change on accuracy grounds: "el código con las cadenas invertidas" for "the code with these strings reversed" is ambiguous in a file where "inversión de bit" is the established rendering of bit flip (it reads as bit-flipped rather than read-backwards), and "son por tanto completamente invisibles para ambos" reverses the direction of English "they're completely oblivious to both" (it is the generators that are blind to the Z errors, not the generators that are invisible). Plus a spelling slip "Como se menciónó" (should be "mencionó") and a cluster of stiff German/English-shaped connectives ("Pues al medir el síndrome…", "De hecho, sin embargo,", "Correspondientemente, sea …") that a Spanish technical writer would recast. None of these would make a learner form a false belief about CSS codes, so this stays below FAIL.

examples.source: (Sometimes the [7,4,3]-Hamming code is understood to mean the code with these strings reversed, but we'll take it to be the code containing the strings shown here.)
examples.suggested: …el código con las cadenas leídas en orden inverso…
examples.translation: (A veces se entiende por código de Hamming $[7,4,3]$ el código con las cadenas invertidas, pero aquí consideramos el código con las cadenas que se muestran a continuación.)
examples.why: "reversed" = bit order reversed, but this file uses "invertir/inversión" throughout for bit FLIPS ("error de inversión de bit"), so "cadenas invertidas" reads as bit-complemented strings — a different (wrong) code.

examples.source: …so they're completely oblivious to both, and likewise for X stabilizer generators, errors, and corrections.
examples.suggested: — por tanto son completamente insensibles a ambos (no los detectan) — y lo mismo ocurre con los generadores de estabilizador $X$…
examples.translation: — son por tanto completamente invisibles para ambos — y lo mismo ocurre recíprocamente con los generadores de estabilizador $X$, errores y correcciones.
examples.why: Direction is swapped: the English says the generators do not notice the errors/corrections; the Spanish says the generators are invisible to them. Also "recíprocamente" adds a symmetry nuance the English "likewise" does not carry.

examples.source: This is because, when the syndrome is measured, an arbitrary error on this number of qubits effectively collapses probabilistically…
examples.suggested: Esto se debe a que, al medir el síndrome, un error arbitrario sobre ese número de qubits colapsa, en la práctica, de forma probabilística…
examples.translation: Pues al medir el síndrome, un error arbitrario en ese número de qubits colapsa probabilísticamente…
examples.why: Sentence-initial "Pues" as a causal connective is a calque (German "Denn"/English "This is because") that a Spanish technical writer would not use here; "effectively" is also dropped. Same stiffness in "De hecho, sin embargo," (line 295) and "Correspondientemente, sea …" (line 322).

examples.source: As we noted in the previous lesson, the code space for this code is the one-dimensional space spanned by the |phi+> Bell state.
examples.suggested: Como se mencionó en la lección anterior, …
examples.translation: Como se menciónó en la lección anterior, el espacio de código de este código es el espacio unidimensional generado por el estado de Bell $\vert\phi^+\rangle$.
examples.why: Spelling slip: "menciónó" carries a stray accent on the stem; correct form is "mencionó". Cosmetic but visible in body prose.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every probability (9/25, 16/25, 2/3, 1/3, 3/7, 2/7), every conditional ("si (1) fuera un estado producto…"), the non-commutativity caveat and the "no hay manera análoga" reduced-state limitation all match the English, and core terms are correct and consistent (estado producto, entrelazamiento, producto tensorial, medición de base estándar, matriz unitaria, transpuesta conjugada, compuerta Fredkin/Toffoli). What a native editor would change: (a) the reverse/inverse wordplay collapses — "Esto representa la *inversa*, o en términos matemáticos el *inverso*" renders both English words with the same Spanish root, so the sentence reads as a tautology and the pedagogical contrast is lost; (b) several English-syntax calques survive — "cualquier vector complejo en absoluto" (en absoluto is negative-polarity in Spanish), "A lo largo de líneas similares", "no puede posiblemente depender", "todos los cuatro estados de Bell", "en acuerdo con" for "in agreement with"; (c) "collect terms/collect the systems" is rendered "recopilar términos" / "recopilar los sistemas juntos", where the mathematical verb is "agrupar"; (d) register wobbles — "suponga que" (usted) appears twice against the dominant "supongamos" and one "Supón que". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: This represents the *reverse*, or in mathematical terms the *inverse*, of the original operation
examples.suggested: Esto representa la *reversa* de la operación original, o en términos matemáticos su *inversa*
examples.translation: Esto representa la *inversa*, o en términos matemáticos el *inverso*, de la operación original
examples.why: English contrasts an everyday word (reverse) with the mathematical term (inverse); Spanish uses the same root twice, so the clarifying contrast becomes a tautology and the teaching point disappears.

examples.source: or indeed any complex vector at all having entries corresponding to the four classical states
examples.suggested: o de hecho cualquier vector complejo que tenga entradas correspondientes a los cuatro estados clásicos
examples.translation: o de hecho cualquier vector complejo en absoluto que tenga entradas correspondientes a los cuatro estados clásicos
examples.why: 'en absoluto' is a negative-polarity intensifier in Spanish ('not at all'); calqued from English 'at all' it reads as broken usage a native technical writer would never produce.

examples.source: Along similar lines, if an operation represented by a unitary matrix U is applied to Y
examples.suggested: De manera similar, si se aplica una operación representada por una matriz unitaria $U$ a $\mathsf{Y}$
examples.translation: A lo largo de líneas similares, si se aplica una operación representada por una matriz unitaria $U$ a $\mathsf{Y}$
examples.why: Word-for-word calque of the English idiom; 'a lo largo de líneas similares' is not Spanish discourse marker usage.

examples.source: We can now re-order the kets and collect terms as follows / collect the systems together as
examples.suggested: …y agrupar términos… / …agrupar los sistemas como…
examples.translation: Ahora podemos reordenar los kets y recopilar términos… / es más conveniente recopilar los sistemas juntos como
examples.why: 'recopilar' means to compile/gather documentation; the mathematical operation of collecting like terms is 'agrupar (términos)' in Spanish math writing.

examples.source: suppose that |phi> is a quantum state vector … suppose that X and Y are systems
examples.suggested: supongamos que … / supón que …
examples.translation: suponga que $\vert \phi \rangle$ es un vector de estado cuántico … Por ejemplo, suponga que $\mathsf{X}$ y $\mathsf{Y}$ son sistemas
examples.why: 'suponga' is the usted imperative, breaking the file's informal-tú convention used elsewhere ('Supón que X y Y son sistemas', 'Nota que…', 'supongamos').

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (3p²(1−p)+p³, "pour des valeurs de p inférieures à un demi ... le code *diminue* cette probabilité" vs the parenthetical "*supérieures* à un demi ... *augmente*", "au plus un basculement de bit", "un nombre impair d'erreurs de basculement de phase", "insensible aux erreurs de basculement de bit"), and syndrome/correction tables and the no-cloning caveat are correct. Two editorial slips: the central term is rendered "code répétitif" (lit. "repetitive code") where the established French term is "code à répétition" — recognizable, so not misleading, but nonstandard and used file-wide; and near the end "the single qubit state α|0⟩+β|1⟩" becomes "l'état de qubit à un bit", which nonsensically attaches "à un bit" to a qubit state instead of saying "l'état à un seul qubit". Minor also: "supposons que notre objectif soit ... et que nous pouvons transmettre" breaks the subjunctive sequence ("puissions"), and "a perfect, unitary operation" is compressed to "une opération parfaitement unitaire" (two adjectives collapsed into an adverb+adjective).

examples.source: repetition codes / the 3-bit repetition code
examples.suggested: codes à répétition / le code à répétition à 3 bits
examples.translation: codes répétitifs / le code répétitif à 3 bits
examples.why: The conventional French term in coding-theory and QEC literature is « code à répétition ». « Code répétitif » back-translates as "repetitive code" — understandable, so not misleading, but it is not the term a French quantum engineer would write, and it is used consistently file-wide so the fix is mechanical.

examples.source: the net effect is that the single qubit state $\alpha\vert 0\rangle + \beta \vert 1\rangle$ is encoded as
examples.suggested: l'effet net est que l'état à un seul qubit $\alpha\vert 0\rangle + \beta \vert 1\rangle$ est encodé en
examples.translation: l'effet net est que l'état de qubit à un bit $\alpha\vert 0\rangle + \beta \vert 1\rangle$ est encodé en
examples.why: "single qubit" has been split into "de qubit" + "à un bit", producing a state described as being "one bit" wide — a bit/qubit conflation in a lesson whose whole point is the difference between classical bits and qubits. Recognizable in context, hence minor, but a native technical editor would not leave it.

examples.source: suppose that our goal is to communicate a single bit ... and we're able to transmit bits through a so-called *binary symmetric channel*
examples.suggested: supposons que notre objectif soit de communiquer un seul bit ... et que nous puissions transmettre des bits via ce qu'on appelle un *canal binaire symétrique*
examples.translation: supposons que notre objectif soit de communiquer un seul bit ... et que nous pouvons transmettre des bits via un *canal binaire symétrique*
examples.why: The second coordinated clause after « supposons que » drops back to the indicative (« pouvons ») where the first correctly used the subjunctive (« soit »); a native writer would keep « puissions ». The hedge "so-called", which flags the term as jargon being introduced, is also dropped — note the same hedge IS kept later for « ce qu'on appelle la *discrétisation des erreurs* », so the file is inconsistent with itself.

examples.source: it's also reasonable to question the assumption that an error takes the form of a perfect, unitary operation
examples.suggested: ... l'hypothèse selon laquelle une erreur prend la forme d'une opération unitaire parfaite
examples.translation: il est également raisonnable de remettre en question l'hypothèse selon laquelle une erreur prend la forme d'une opération parfaitement unitaire
examples.why: English lists two independent properties (perfect AND unitary); the French turns "perfect" into an adverb modifying "unitary", so the sentence now questions only the exactness of unitarity rather than the idealization as a whole. The nuance is small and does not mislead about the physics, but the emphasis is flattened.

editor_note: No misleading content: the technical chain (Toffoli = controlled-controlled-NOT, garbage qubits, running $R$ in reverse, the $Q(\vert y\rangle\vert 0^k\rangle\vert x\rangle)$ identity, the invertibility caveat "ce n'est pas unitaire quand $f$ ne l'est pas") is faithful and complete, so this is not a FAIL. What a native technical editor would change: (1) "les qubits sont ordonnés par signification croissante de haut en bas" renders bit *significance* as "signification" — the French convention is "par poids croissant"/"par ordre de significativité croissante"; "signification" means "meaning" and is simply not the term; (2) SWAP is rendered two different ways in the same file — "portes SWAP" (§ gate-by-gate) then "portes de permutation" (final paragraph), for the same English "swap gates"; (3) "larger quantum computations" is calqued twice as "calculs quantiques plus larges" (an anglicism; French wants "plus vastes"/"plus importants"); (4) the XOR sentence "on ne conserve pas une copie de l'entrée et ne lui applique pas un XOR vers une chaîne arbitraire" is stiff and re-anchors the XOR onto the *input* rather than the output, plus "appliquer un XOR vers" is not idiomatic. Register convention holds (nous/on throughout, no vous/veuillez).

examples.source: the qubits are ordered in increasing significance from top to bottom
examples.suggested: les qubits sont ordonnés par poids croissant de haut en bas
examples.translation: les qubits sont ordonnés par signification croissante de haut en bas
examples.why: "Significance" here is bit weight (poids binaire / significativité), not "signification" (= meaning). The literal rendering is not the French domain term and leaves the ordering criterion vague, though the top-to-bottom direction still comes through.

examples.source: SWAP gates … n swap gates
examples.suggested: use "portes SWAP" in both places
examples.translation: portes SWAP … $n$ portes de permutation
examples.why: The same English term is rendered two ways within one file; the last-paragraph "portes de permutation" no longer visibly ties back to the SWAP construction (three CNOTs) introduced earlier.

examples.source: larger quantum computations
examples.suggested: calculs quantiques plus vastes / plus importants
examples.translation: calculs quantiques plus larges
examples.why: "Plus larges" is a calque of English "larger"; in French "large" is width, not size/scope. A native technical writer would write "plus vastes" or "de plus grande envergure".

examples.source: because we're not keeping a copy of the input around and XORing it to an arbitrary string, we're replacing x by f(x)
examples.suggested: car on ne conserve pas de copie de l'entrée et on n'effectue pas de XOR du résultat avec une chaîne arbitraire : on remplace $x$ par $f(x)$
examples.translation: car on ne conserve pas une copie de l'entrée et ne lui applique pas un XOR vers une chaîne arbitraire, on remplace $x$ par $f(x)$
examples.why: "appliquer un XOR vers" is not idiomatic French (one writes "effectuer un XOR avec"), and the pronoun "lui" attaches the XOR to the input rather than to the computed output, blurring the contrast with the $\vert y \oplus f(x)\rangle$ behaviour of $Q$ shown just above.

editor_note: Mathematically faithful throughout — every quantifier, condition and "si et seulement si" matches the English, the POVM development ("matrices semi-définies positives", "canal de déphasage complet", "représentation de Choi", "état classique-quantique") is correct and consistent, and the FR even repairs the English slip "a pure state divided by one-half" to the correct "un état pur divisé par deux". Nothing misleads. What a native technical editor would still change is a layer of calqued phrasing: matrix elements are called "entrées" (diagonales / hors-diagonale) rather than the standard "coefficients"/"éléments", which also collides with "entrées" used for channel inputs two paragraphs earlier ("les entrées sont des matrices"); "les probabilités somment à 1" and "Une façon d'argumenter ce fait" are anglicisms; "grâce au fait que" is used twice where English has "owing to the fact that" ("grâce à" wrongly implies benefit — "du fait que" is meant); "En traçant le système de sortie Y" under-renders "tracing out" (standard: "en prenant la trace partielle sur"); and "nous avons avec probabilité p(a) que Y est dans l'état classique…" reproduces English word order no French author would write. Register is correctly informal (Rappelle-toi, comme bon te semble, Essaie de le montrer).

examples.source: it zeros out all of the off-diagonal entries of an input matrix and leaves the diagonal alone
examples.suggested: il annule tous les coefficients hors-diagonaux d'une matrice d'entrée et laisse la diagonale inchangée
examples.translation: il annule toutes les entrées hors-diagonale d'une matrice d'entrée et laisse la diagonale inchangée
examples.why: "entrées" for matrix entries is a calque (French uses "coefficients"/"éléments"), and it clashes with "entrées" already used for the channel's inputs ("les entrées sont des matrices", §Les mesures comme canaux). Used consistently this way in four places, including "les entrées diagonales de Φ(ρ)" and "ayant des entrées en correspondance avec l'état classique".

examples.source: ensures that the probabilities sum to 1
examples.suggested: garantit que la somme des probabilités vaut 1
examples.translation: garantit que les probabilités somment à 1
examples.why: "sommer à" is a direct anglicism; French says "garantit que la somme des probabilités vaut 1" or "que les probabilités s'additionnent pour donner 1".

examples.source: owing to the fact that this expression is linear in ρ / owing to the fact that the trace of the product ... is always nonnegative
examples.suggested: du fait que cette expression est linéaire en ρ / car la trace du produit ... est toujours non négative
examples.translation: grâce au fait que cette expression est linéaire en ρ / grâce au fait que la trace du produit ... est toujours non négative
examples.why: "grâce à" carries a notion of benefit and is not a neutral causal connector; in a proof the correct register is "du fait que" / "car". Occurs twice.

examples.source: Tracing out the output system Y (which is the system on the right) yields
examples.suggested: En prenant la trace partielle sur le système de sortie Y (le système de droite), on obtient
examples.translation: En traçant le système de sortie Y (le système de droite), on obtient
examples.why: "tracer" in French means to draw/plot; the established term for "trace out" is "prendre la trace partielle sur". The adjacent formula Tr_Y makes the meaning recoverable, so this is imperfect rather than misleading.

examples.source: For each measurement outcome a, we have with probability p(a) = ... that Y is in the classical state |a⟩⟨a| and Z is in the state
examples.suggested: Pour chaque résultat de mesure a, avec probabilité p(a) = ..., Y est dans l'état classique |a⟩⟨a| et Z dans l'état
examples.translation: Pour chaque résultat de mesure a, nous avons avec probabilité p(a) = ... que Y est dans l'état classique |a⟩⟨a| et Z est dans l'état
examples.why: "nous avons avec probabilité ... que" reproduces the English clause order verbatim; no French technical writer would build the sentence this way.

examples.source: or that the system is immediately discarded once the measurement is made
examples.suggested: ou que le système est immédiatement écarté / jeté une fois la mesure effectuée
examples.translation: ou que le système est immédiatement mis de côté une fois la mesure effectuée
examples.why: "mis de côté" (set aside, kept for later) slightly softens "discarded", which here reinforces the point that the measured system is gone. The surrounding sentence ("détruit le système quantique lui-même") preserves the intuition, so the softening is minor.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every claim, quantity and caveat matches the English (five cut edges, four true max-cut solutions, the fourth identified solution being wrong with only four cuts, 32 possible bitstrings, two layers, γ=π/2 / β=π), the "tu" register holds throughout, and core terms (état fondamental, ansatz, porte Hadamard, chaînes de bits, transpilation, backend, shots) are correct. The fixable slips are terminological: English "plot" is rendered "graphe" twice ("dans les chaînes de bits du graphe", "À partir de ce graphe"), which collides head-on with "graphe" used ~20 times in this file for the max-cut graph — it should be "graphique"/"tracé"; "two-local Pauli ZZ operators" becomes the awkward calque "opérateurs de Pauli ZZ à deux corps locaux"; the primitives are split, with "Estimator" translated ("l'estimateur") but "Sampler" kept English in the same sentence; and "Instruction Set Architecture" is calqued as "architecture d'ensemble d'instructions" instead of the conventional "architecture du jeu d'instructions". Also minor: the article on "Hamiltonien" alternates between elided ("l'Hamiltonien d'Ising") and non-elided ("le Hamiltonien mixer", "ce Hamiltonien", "du Hamiltonien final"). None of these would make a learner form a false belief.

examples.source: (Remember – the order of the qubits is reversed in the plot bitstrings!) … From this plot, we can take the most likely bitstring
examples.suggested: … dans les chaînes de bits du graphique ! … À partir de ce graphique, nous pouvons prendre …
examples.translation: l'ordre des qubits est inversé dans les chaînes de bits du graphe ! … À partir de ce graphe, nous pouvons prendre la chaîne de bits la plus probable
examples.why: "plot" (the histogram) is rendered "graphe", the exact word this file uses throughout for the max-cut graph itself; the reader momentarily reads it as the node/edge graph. "graphique" or "tracé" removes the collision.

examples.source: we need to rewrite it in terms of two-local Pauli ZZ operators
examples.suggested: nous devons le réécrire en termes d'opérateurs de Pauli ZZ à deux corps (two-local)
examples.translation: nous devons le réécrire en termes d'opérateurs de Pauli ZZ à deux corps locaux
examples.why: "à deux corps locaux" is a calque that parses oddly in French — "locaux" ends up qualifying "corps". The conventional rendering is "à deux corps" (opérateurs deux-locaux), i.e. acting on two qubits.

examples.source: A single primitive request of the Estimator or Sampler primitive is made without a context manager.
examples.suggested: Une seule requête à la primitive Estimator ou Sampler est effectuée sans gestionnaire de contexte.
examples.translation: Une seule requête primitive de l'estimateur ou du sampler est effectuée sans gestionnaire de contexte.
examples.why: The two Qiskit primitive class names are handled inconsistently in one sentence: Estimator is translated and lower-cased, Sampler is kept English. Both are API class names and should stay capitalized in English.

examples.source: Such circuits are said to be written in the backend's Instruction Set Architecture (ISA).
examples.suggested: De tels circuits sont dits écrits dans l'architecture du jeu d'instructions (ISA) du backend.
examples.translation: De tels circuits sont dits écrits dans l'architecture d'ensemble d'instructions (ISA) du backend.
examples.why: "ensemble d'instructions" is a word-for-word calque; the established French computing term for "instruction set" is "jeu d'instructions".

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — no inverted conditions, no swapped quantities, no dropped caveats; the delicate passages (the "no classical computer, simulator, or GPU" warning, the gradient-washed-out-by-errors discussion, the success:False / nfev=10 explanation, "not necessarily the last value calculated") all land correctly, and informal "tu" holds consistently. The one real defect is structural: the third bullet of the session/options list is duplicated — line 265 is the raw untranslated English source line ("Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization, …") sitting immediately above its French rendering on line 266, so a French reader meets the same bullet twice, once in English. Two smaller slips: "pass manager" is rendered two ways inside one sentence ("génère un gestionnaire de passes en utilisant des pass managers prédéfinis", line 148, and again "pass manager" at line 264), and "a highly-entangled 127-qubit quantum computer" becomes "ordinateur quantique à 127 qubits fortement intriqués" (line 202), where the plural agreement moves "highly-entangled" onto the qubits rather than the machine. Note also that the French bullet's link target was changed to /guides/configure-error-mitigation while the English points at /guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques.

examples.source: * Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization, Estimator has built-in settings for resilience against errors, corresponding to different approaches to error mitigation. To learn about resilience level settings, refer to the [documentation](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques).
examples.suggested: Keep only the French bullet ("* Résilience intégrée d'Estimator : …") and delete the leftover English line; restore the English link target /guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques.
examples.translation:
* Estimator's built-in resilience: As with optimization, Estimator has built-in settings for resilience against errors, corresponding to different approaches to error mitigation. To learn about resilience level settings, refer to the  [documentation](/guides/error-mitigation-and-suppression-techniques).
* Résilience intégrée d'Estimator : Comme pour l'optimisation, Estimator dispose de paramètres intégrés pour la résilience aux erreurs, correspondant à différentes approches de mitigation des erreurs. Pour en savoir plus sur les paramètres de niveau de résilience, consulte la [documentation](/guides/configure-error-mitigation).
examples.why: The untranslated English source bullet was left in place alongside its French translation, so the list has a duplicated item and one bullet is not in French at all. The surviving French bullet also points at a different guide URL than the source.

examples.source: The code below generates a mass manager using preset pass managers from `qiskit.transpiler`. … because we have already transpiled our circuit using the pass manager above
examples.suggested: Use one rendering throughout, e.g. "génère un pass manager en utilisant les pass managers prédéfinis de `qiskit.transpiler`".
examples.translation: Le code ci-dessous génère un gestionnaire de passes en utilisant des pass managers prédéfinis issus de `qiskit.transpiler`. … car nous avons déjà transpilé notre circuit à l'aide du pass manager ci-dessus
examples.why: "pass manager" is rendered both as "gestionnaire de passes" and kept as "pass manager" within a single sentence, which makes the Qiskit API object (PassManager) look like two different things.

examples.source: no classical computer, simulator, or GPU can accurately simulate the full functionality of a highly-entangled 127-qubit quantum computer
examples.suggested: … d'un ordinateur quantique à 127 qubits fortement intriqué (or: … d'un ordinateur quantique de 127 qubits dans un état fortement intriqué)
examples.translation: aucun ordinateur classique, simulateur ou GPU ne peut simuler avec précision la pleine fonctionnalité d'un ordinateur quantique à 127 qubits fortement intriqués
examples.why: Plural agreement shifts "highly-entangled" from the computer onto the qubits; the English qualifies the machine's overall state, and the French phrasing reads as a calque of the English compound adjective.

editor_note: Meaning is faithful throughout — I checked every load-bearing claim (CNOT « inverse le qubit cible uniquement lorsque le qubit de contrôle est |1⟩ », les 75 % de chance de devenir |0⟩, Little Endian « le qubit 0 est le bit le plus à droite », profondeur 4 / profondeur 5 portes de mesure incluses, « les circuits de faible profondeur ont moins d'erreurs… Les circuits très profonds ne le sont pas ») and found no inverted condition, swapped quantity, dropped caveat or hallucinated sentence; the "tu" register holds from the description line to the summary. What a native technical editor would still change is a handful of calques: "two-dimensional complex inner product space" becomes "espace produit intérieur complexe à deux dimensions", a literal rendering of *inner product* — French says "espace préhilbertien complexe" or "muni d'un produit scalaire hermitien"; "basic building blocks" becomes "blocs de construction fondamentaux" where a French writer would say "les briques de base"; and "transformer les entrées dont on dispose en les sorties dont on a besoin" has an awkward "en les". Two smaller slips: the doubled "un état intriqué particulier qui est particulièrement important" (§4.3), and "job" rendered as "travail" ("les résultats du travail", "le statut du travail"), where French Qiskit material normally keeps *job* or uses "tâche". None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: the state of a quantum bit is a unit vector in a two-dimensional complex inner product space with an orthonormal basis of $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$
examples.suggested: l'état d'un bit quantique est un vecteur unitaire d'un espace préhilbertien complexe de dimension deux, muni de la base orthonormée $|0\rangle$, $|1\rangle$
examples.translation: l'état d'un bit quantique est un vecteur unitaire dans un espace produit intérieur complexe à deux dimensions, avec une base orthonormale formée de $|0\rangle$ et $|1\rangle$
examples.why: "espace produit intérieur" is a word-for-word calque of *inner product space*; the established French term is "espace préhilbertien" (or "espace vectoriel muni d'un produit scalaire hermitien"). Recognizable, so not misleading, but no French mathematician writes it this way. Same family: "produit extérieur" for *outer product* (line ~365) is defensible but reads as a calque next to it.

examples.source: we need to manipulate them in order to turn the inputs we have into the outputs we need
examples.suggested: il faut les manipuler pour transformer les entrées dont on dispose en les sorties voulues → better: "…pour obtenir, à partir des entrées dont on dispose, les sorties dont on a besoin"
examples.translation: il faut les manipuler pour transformer les entrées dont on dispose en les sorties dont on a besoin
examples.why: "transformer … en les sorties" is ungainly French — "en" before a definite article is avoided in this construction. English sentence shape carried over verbatim; a native writer would restructure.

examples.source: Bits, gates, and circuits are the basic building blocks of quantum computing.
examples.suggested: Les bits, les portes et les circuits sont les briques de base du calcul quantique.
examples.translation: Les bits, les portes et les circuits sont les blocs de construction fondamentaux du calcul quantique.
examples.why: "blocs de construction" is the literal calque of *building blocks*; French technical prose uses "briques de base" (or "éléments de base"). Opening sentence of the lesson, so the translationese is prominent.

examples.source: The job_id is used to check the execution status and results of the job later. / You can also check the job status from your IBM Quantum dashboard
examples.suggested: …le statut d'exécution et les résultats du job ultérieurement. / …vérifier le statut du job depuis ton tableau de bord IBM Quantum
examples.translation: Le job_id est utilisé pour vérifier le statut d'exécution et les résultats du travail ultérieurement. / Tu peux également vérifier le statut du travail depuis ton tableau de bord IBM Quantum
examples.why: French Qiskit/IBM Quantum material keeps "job" (or uses "tâche"); "travail" reads as a generic dictionary rendering and sits oddly beside the untranslated identifier `job_id` in the very same sentence. Understandable, so MINOR only.

editor_note: One genuinely misleading error in the "5k challenge" section: EN "Imagine what is possible with 5,000 quantum gates in a single computation" is rendered "Immagina cosa è possibile con 5.000 circuiti quantistici in un'unica computazione" — gates became circuits, which destroys the whole point of the section (the 5k challenge is about 5,000 gates i.e. circuit depth, not 5,000 circuits) and contradicts the preceding sentence about "numero preciso di qubit e la profondità". The same paragraph also carries a grammar slip, "meno importante del sfruttare la potenza" (should be "dello sfruttare"/"che sfruttare"). Otherwise the file is faithful and reads naturally: the NYC tourist analogy (lines 78-84) is preserved intact with the fixed-space/fixed-time conditions correct, terminology is solid ("qubit transmon superconduttore", "tassi di errore", "codice di Gross", "qubit a ioni intrappolati"), and the informal "tu" register holds throughout ("Se fai parte", "considera", "Immagina"). Minor: "expectation value" → "valore di aspettativa" (conventional Italian is "valore di aspettazione"/"valore atteso"), and Quantum Volume is capitalized consistently except once as "quantum volume" (line 88).

examples.source: Imagine what is possible with 5,000 quantum gates in a single computation.
examples.suggested: Immagina cosa è possibile con 5.000 gate quantistici in un'unica computazione.
examples.translation: Immagina cosa è possibile con 5.000 circuiti quantistici in un'unica computazione.
examples.why: "gates" was replaced by "circuiti". The section is the 5k challenge — 5,000 gates in ONE computation (depth). Saying 5,000 circuits teaches the opposite scale concept and clashes with the immediately preceding sentence about qubit count and circuit depth, and with the next sentence about running circuits.

examples.source: But the precise number of qubits and depth on each is less important than leveraging the power of the combination.
examples.suggested: Ma il numero preciso di qubit e la profondità di ciascuno conta meno che sfruttare la potenza della combinazione.
examples.translation: Ma il numero preciso di qubit e la profondità di ciascuno è meno importante del sfruttare la potenza della combinazione.
examples.why: "del sfruttare" is ungrammatical (elision/article error); a native technical writer would use "che sfruttare" or "dello sfruttare".

examples.source: a property of the system called its expectation value
examples.suggested: una proprietà del sistema chiamata valore di aspettazione (o valore atteso)
examples.translation: una proprietà del sistema chiamata valore di aspettativa
examples.why: The established Italian domain term is "valore di aspettazione" / "valore atteso"; "valore di aspettativa" is a literal calque, recognizable but not the conventional rendering.

examples.source: and quality by quantum volume
examples.suggested: e la qualità tramite il Quantum Volume
examples.translation: e la qualità tramite il quantum volume
examples.why: Every other occurrence in the file keeps the capitalized proper-metric form "Quantum Volume"; this single lowercase instance breaks within-file consistency.

editor_note: Nothing in the file misleads on the physics/crypto: the four CHF properties, the $2^n$ vs $2^{n/2}$ vs $2^{n/3}$ / $\tilde{O}(2^{2n/5})$ scalings, the 256→128-bit Grover argument and the QRAM caveat all survive intact, and "infeasible" is rendered consistently as "computazionalmente impossibile". Three things a native technical editor would still change. (1) The bolded property name in item 4 reads "**Inettività approssimata**" — "inettività" is a real Italian word meaning ineptitude; the correct "iniettività approssimata" appears at the end of the same paragraph, so the concept stays recognizable but the headword is misspelled and self-inconsistent. (2) The summary sentence "le lunghe lunghezze di hash già in uso oggi significa che..." has a number-agreement error (significa/significano) plus the clumsy "lunghe lunghezze". (3) "scaling" is rendered "scalabilità" (scalability) twice in the BHT section where the sense is asymptotic behaviour ("andamento"/"comportamento asintotico"); "with high probability" is flattened to "ragionevolmente certi" and "cheaply" to "in modo efficiente", both dropping a shade of the original qualifier.

examples.source: **Approximate injectivity:** ... This characteristic is known as approximate injectivity.
examples.suggested: **Iniettività approssimata:** ...
examples.translation: **Inettività approssimata:** ... Questa caratteristica è nota come iniettività approssimata.
examples.why: The bolded term is misspelled as 'inettività' (= ineptitude, a different real Italian word) while the correct 'iniettività' appears in the same paragraph — an internal split of the property's own name.

examples.source: the long hash lengths already in use today means that modern cryptographic hashing algorithms ... are likely to remain secure
examples.suggested: le notevoli lunghezze di hash già in uso oggi fanno sì che i moderni algoritmi di hashing crittografico ... rimarranno probabilmente sicuri
examples.translation: le lunghe lunghezze di hash già in uso oggi significa che i moderni algoritmi di hashing crittografico ... rimarranno probabilmente sicuri
examples.why: Subject–verb agreement error ('lunghezze ... significa') plus the redundant 'lunghe lunghezze'; no native technical writer would leave this in the closing paragraph.

examples.source: affords a theoretical scaling of $O(2^{n/3})$ ... the realizable scaling is $\tilde{O}(2^{2n/5})$
examples.suggested: offre un andamento asintotico teorico di $O(2^{n/3})$ ... l'andamento realizzabile è $\tilde{O}(2^{2n/5})$
examples.translation: offre una scalabilità teorica di $O(2^{n/3})$ ... la scalabilità realizzabile è $\tilde{O}(2^{2n/5})$
examples.why: 'Scalabilità' means scalability (a system property); here 'scaling' denotes asymptotic complexity growth, normally 'andamento/comportamento asintotico' in Italian complexity writing.

examples.source: If the two digests match, we can be confident with high probability that the data is identical to the original.
examples.suggested: Se i due digest corrispondono, possiamo essere certi con probabilità elevata che il dato sia identico all'originale.
examples.translation: Se i due digest corrispondono, possiamo essere ragionevolmente certi che il dato sia identico all'originale.
examples.why: 'With high probability' is a quantitative hedge that contrasts deliberately with the 'possiamo essere certi' of the next bullet; 'ragionevolmente certi' flattens the probabilistic asymmetry the passage is teaching.

editor_note: No semantic drift or hallucination: every quantitative and conditional claim survives intact (X-vs-CNOT commutation rules, "al massimo un blocco subisca un numero dispari di essi", punto di pareggio 0.0323, "peggio di nessun codice quando p è maggiore di un mezzo"), terminology is correct and consistent (codice interno/esterno, misurazione della sindrome, degenerazione, qubit logico/fisici, bit-flip/phase-flip kept in English as the field does), and the informal register holds ("considera l'esempio"). What a native technical editor would still change: a grammar slip at "i gate $X$ su qualsiasi dei nove qubit" (needs "su uno qualsiasi dei nove qubit", the correct form used elsewhere in the same file); the calque "Come si scopre" for "As it turns out"; a mixed-tense hypothetical "se non avessimo utilizzato il codice, il nostro unico qubit subirebbe..."; and the closing "non è effettivamente un codice molto efficiente", which narrows the English "isn't actually a very good code in practical terms" from overall quality to efficiency. None of these would mislead a learner.

examples.source: $X$ gates on any of the nine qubits used for the encoding commute with all of the gates
examples.suggested: i gate $X$ su uno qualsiasi dei nove qubit usati per la codifica commutano con tutti i gate
examples.translation: i gate $X$ su qualsiasi dei nove qubit usati per la codifica commutano con tutti i gate
examples.why: "su qualsiasi dei" is ungrammatical; Italian needs "su uno qualsiasi dei" — the form the same file already uses correctly at lines 85, 108 and 169.

examples.source: As it turns out, nothing different needs to be done in this situation
examples.suggested: A quanto pare, in questa situazione non occorre fare nulla di diverso
examples.translation: Come si scopre, in questa situazione non occorre fare nulla di diverso
examples.why: "Come si scopre" is a literal calque of "as it turns out" that no Italian technical writer would use as a discourse connective.

examples.source: it should be acknowledged that it isn't actually a very good code in practical terms
examples.suggested: va riconosciuto che, in termini pratici, non è in realtà un codice molto buono
examples.translation: va riconosciuto che in termini pratici non è effettivamente un codice molto efficiente
examples.why: "efficiente" narrows the English judgement about overall code quality (rate/distance/practicality) to efficiency alone; a mild softening of the closing verdict.

examples.source: if we didn't bother to use the code, our one and only qubit would suffer a similar fate
examples.suggested: se non ci prendessimo la briga di usare il codice, il nostro unico qubit subirebbe un destino simile
examples.translation: se non avessimo utilizzato il codice, il nostro unico qubit subirebbe un destino simile
examples.why: Mixed-time hypothetical (past subjunctive protasis + present conditional apodosis) reads off in Italian; the source is a present counterfactual, and "bother to" is also dropped.
